'''''Euphorbia ammak''''', commonly known as '''giant milk bush''', '''African candelabra''' and '''candelabra spurge''',<ref name=llifle>[http://www.llifle.com/Encyclopedia/SUCCULENTS/Family/Euphorbiaceae/18545/Euphorbia_ammak Euphorbia ammak Schweinf.] by www.llifle.com. Retrieved 10 November 2024.</ref> is a species of [[plant]] in the family [[Euphorbiaceae]] native to the [[Arabian Peninsula]]. 

As most other succulent members of the genus ''Euphorbia'', its trade is regulated under Appendix II of [[CITES]].<ref name="Species+">{{Cite web 
|title=Species+|url=https://www.speciesplus.net/species#/taxon_concepts/16470/legal |access-date=7 February 2023}}</ref> In 1998, the plant was assessed for The [[IUCN Red List of Threatened Species]] and was listed as [[Vulnerable species|Vulnerable]].<ref name="iucn status 17 November 2021"/>

==Description==
[[File:Starr-090428-6455-Euphorbia ammak-flowers-Kula-Maui (24325925553).jpg|thumb|left|Emerging flowers]]
[[File:大戟閣 Euphorbia ammak Schw. - panoramio.jpg|thumb|left|Growth structure]]
[[File:Euphorbia ammak variegata ies.jpg|thumb|left|Variegata]]
It forms a tree up to 10 meters high with upright and curved main shoots. The square [[Shoot (botany)|shoots]] reach a thickness of 12 to 15 centimeters. On the wing-like edges there are curved teeth at a distance of up to 1 centimeter from each other. The inverted triangular [[Thorns, spines, and prickles|thorn]] shields stand individually. Thorns up to 1 centimeter long are formed. In a suitable climate (humid and warm at the same time) the leaves appear at the tops of the branches.<ref name=dave>[https://davesgarden.com/guides/articles/view/236 Euphorbias for landscaping - the cold-hardy columnar, tree species] by Geoff Stein from Dave's Garden. April 8, 2014. Retrieved November 10, 2024.</ref> 

On seedlings, the lanceolate leaves are up to 40 millimeters long and up to 7 millimeters wide; on younger shoots of older plants the leaves are not so large. Branches initially about 60 cm long, rising vertically upwards, 4-5-ribbed, deeply furrowed, dark green; ribs thick, wavy; young non-flowering shoots with a pair of thorns at a distance of 1 cm from each other. The branches are covered with spines around 1 cm long. Thorns dark brown, 1 cm long, in the form of horns or inverted triangles. Its short trunk, which is 10-15 cm thick, resembles a [[cactus]], and its inversely [[conical]] crown makes it look like a [[candelabrum]], hence one of its common names.<ref name=dave/><ref name=llifle/>

===Inflorescence=== 
The [[inflorescence]] is formed from individual, simple and almost [[Sessility (botany)|sessile]] cymes. The [[cyathia]] reach about 10 millimeters in diameter. The [[nectar]] glands are elliptical and the [[Ovary (botany)|ovary]] has a three-lobed, slit [[perianth]]. The deeply lobed fruit is on a thick, 9 to 14 millimeter long [[Pedicel (botany)|stalk]] and is 9 millimeters long and 14 millimeters wide. The almost round and smooth seed reaches 3 millimeters in diameter.<ref name=dave/>

==Habitat==
It is native to the arid regions of [[Saudi Arabia]] and [[Yemen]]. It grows in shrubby areas between 1000 and 1500 m above sea level, possibly as high as 2500 metres above sea. It is also found in rocky places in plains, on precipitous hillsides and thorny [[scrubland]]s where it has now become rare in its native range (though it remains common in areas in [[Yemen Arab Republic|North Yemen]]).<ref name=dave/>

==Cultivation==
The plant is easy to grow and prefers well drained soil (such as [[clay]] and [[pumice]]) in full sun, though younger plants may perform better indoors as the plant tolerates some shade. Watering should be regular in summer, and the plant should be kept dry in winter. A moderately fast grower and long-living, it matures and becomes large in 3-5 years. In addition to being frost-tender, the plant can be affected by [[mealybugs]] and, very rarely, [[Scale insect|scales]]. Strong winds can also affect the columns. It can easily be propagated by [[cuttings (plants)|cuttings]], though the cutting must callus for a week or two before placed in dry soil.<ref name=llifle/>

In Australia, the plant has adapted well in coastal areas.<ref>[https://urbanjunglesydney.com/products/euphorbia-ammak-xl?srsltid=AfmBOorZCYSL1D8uQ4XNZ3KCaIk_6Fr3bJEunw92gD_gMXGgyNfCIJ70 Euphorbia ammak XL] by UrbanJungleSydney. Retrieved 11 November 2024.</ref> ''Euphorbia ammak 'Variegeta''', a [[variegated]] form found in cultivation, features a creamy-yellow and pale blue-green surface.<ref>[https://www.gardenia.net/plant/euphorbia-ammak-variegata Euphorbia ammak 'Variegata' (Candelabra Spurge)] by Gardenia.net. Retrieved 10 November 2024.</ref>
